summary: PJM files tariff and Reliability Assurance Agreement revisions creating Interim Resource Adequacy Service, a Large Load Registry, definitions of Large Load and New Large Load, and a Variable Resource Requirement curve that excludes new large loads without their own capacity.
ask: Accept the Tariff and RAA revisions by October 12, 2026, effective as requested, with PJM's consent to FERC modifying or severing elements under FPA Section 205.

points.point: IRAS lets PJM prioritize load reduction in zones where new large loads brought no capacity of their own, and only in real-time shortage conditions.
points.quote: a service to be implemented by PJM solely during periods when there are insufficient resources to reliably meet demand in real time operations.

points.point: New large loads avoid IRAS by bringing new capacity, and PJM ties the design to SPP's CHILLS and the June show cause orders.
points.quote: This principle lays the foundation for the IRAS paradigm in PJM that facilitates large load interconnections in a manner similar to the Southwest Power Pool’s (“SPP”) Conditional High Impact Large Load Service

points.point: A Large Load is defined as 50 MW or more of cumulative peak load at a single electrical site, with affiliated facilities within one mile combined.
points.quote: cumulative peak load of 50 megawatts [(“MW”)] or greater at a single electrical site behind one or more points of interconnection

points.point: PJM would direct each distributor zone to cut load up to the MW tied to eligible new large loads, and states choose which load to reduce.
points.quote: each Electric Distributor zone/area may be directed by PJM dispatchers to reduce load up to the MW quantity of capacity attributable to Eligible New Large Loads in that zone/area.

points.point: Compensation for load reduction is capped at 50% of the Non-Performance Charge Rate.
points.quote: 50% of the Non-Performance Charge Rate—as the maximum rate for IRAS performance.

points.point: From 2029/2030 PJM would exclude new large loads without bring-your-own-capacity arrangements from the demand curve.
points.quote: exclude from the VRR Curve New Large Loads, to the extent they do not have arrangements with sufficient BYONC, beginning with the 2029/2030 Delivery Year.

points.point: PJM proposes no end date for IRAS.
points.quote: not proposing an end date to the IRAS program.

points.point: PJM requests an October 12, 2026 effective date for the revisions and registry, with IRAS available from June 1, 2027.
points.quote: make the enclosed proposed Tariff and RAA revisions effective by no later than October 12, 2026

throughLine.text: PJM's separate Section 205 filing, ER26-3515, which cites the June 2026 show cause order. IRAS is a curtailable service for new large loads, and the registry defines Large Load, both themes of E-7.
